annotations.text:
The board, in the product's own kit.

Four figures a person understands at a glance, each with its source printed on the card: output tokens from the agents' own session logs, turns counted from the same files, bounces from the attempt records, held reviews from the stored review-held label and decision gates. Then where the output went by an explicit labelling scheme, then runway per provider from the usage store, then what happened today: every recorded event in time order, with what was written.

Every figure is a field lookup or arithmetic over fields. No text is read for meaning anywhere: a held review is the status_label the review gate writes, not a note that starts with Hold; authors are the plan record's own titles; the log shows notes as written and labels them by their stored kind.

The watcher version adds one chip and one card. Nothing on either board is summarised by a model.

Cost and caching are measured, not estimated: 14 files, 60 MB, under half a second warm and 1.6 s cold; a day of sessions about 8 s; incremental reads under a second. The KPI ledger already ingests the same files behind per-file cursors and is off on this machine; the sheet says what it covers and the one column it lacks.
Every frame was rendered in headless Chrome and sized to its measured content before publishing. Values are lifted from tokens.css, globals.css and the usage panel's stylesheet.
